=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k3 ===
- workflow-templates/validation-harness/python-mongo-flask/Dockerfile.app.j2
  Line or code reference: lines 15-16 — RUN if [ -f "{{ requirements_file }}" ]; then pip install --no-cache-dir -r "{{ requirements_file }}"; fi
  Problem: The sibling template this PR explicitly claims to mirror (README.md line 2183 and the changelog fragment both state the repo-checks template installs requirements "the same way python-mongo-flask already does") still interpolates the schema-unconstrained slots.requirements_file value inside unescaped double quotes. scripts/templates/slot_manifest.schema.json lines 86-120 accept any arbitrary string for slots.additionalProperties, and no pattern constraint exists for requirements_file. The LAST RUN DIFF just fixed this exact defect class in python-mongo-repo-checks/Dockerfile.app.j2 (single-quote + '"'"' escaping at lines 20-21), which confirms the defect is real and in scope, but the flask template that originated the pattern retains it.
  Why it fails at runtime: POSIX shell performs command substitution and parameter expansion inside double quotes, so rendering slots.requirements_file = "req$(cmd).txt" produces a Dockerfile whose RUN line executes cmd via /bin/sh -c during docker build, and a value containing a literal double quote breaks the quoting so the [ -f ] guard and pip install -r operate on the wrong path. The image build then runs attacker/typo-influenced shell or silently skips installing the file the consumer declared — identical runtime failure the autofix editor fixed in the sibling template and justified with "the schema permits arbitrary strings; shell expansion changed valid filename semantics, so the rendering defect was fixed".
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- workflow-templates/validation-harness/python-mongo-flask/Dockerfile.app.j2
  Line or code reference: lines 15-16
  Problem: The sibling template this PR explicitly mirrors (README line 2183 says "like python-mongo-flask", changelog says "the same way python-mongo-flask already does") still interpolates the schema-unconstrained `slots.requirements_file` inside double quotes with no escaping: `RUN if [ -f "{{ requirements_file }}" ]; then \` / `pip install --no-cache-dir -r "{{ requirements_file }}";`. The autofix applied single-quote + apostrophe escaping to `python-mongo-repo-checks` (the template this PR touches), but the identical vulnerability in `python-mongo-flask` was left unchanged. The previous editor rejected extending the fix as "outside this PR's targeted family" — but the PR description, README, and changelog all claim parity with `python-mongo-flask`, and both templates consume the same unconstrained slot through the same Jinja2 renderer.
  Why it fails at runtime: A consumer setting `slots.requirements_file: "req$(cmd).txt"` or a value containing a double quote renders a Dockerfile whose `[ -f ]` guard and `pip install -r` operate on shell-expanded text or a truncated path. The image build silently skips the install or installs from a path the consumer never wrote. This is the exact defect class the LAST RUN DIFF fixed in the sibling template.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
